title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
summary: A trie stores strings character by character along a tree, so words with a common prefix share nodes. insert walks down creating missing children and marks the last node as a word end; search walks down and checks that mark; startsWith only needs the walk to succeed.

complexity.note: Each operation is linear in the word length L.

intuition: Each node has up to 26 children, one per letter.
`isEnd` distinguishes a full word from a prefix ("app" vs "apple").
search and startsWith share the same walk; they differ only in the final check.
pitfalls: Forgetting `isEnd`: then search("app") would be true after inserting only "apple".
Using a HashMap per node is fine for large alphabets but slower for a–z.
input: insert(apple), search(apple), search(app), startsWith(app), insert(app), search(app)
output: [null, null, true, false, true, null, true]

title: Longest Common Prefix
summary: Find the longest prefix shared by every string. Compare column by column: take each character of the first string and check that every other string has the same character at that position. Stop at the first mismatch or when a string runs out.

complexity.note: S = total characters; stops at the first mismatching column.

intuition: The answer can't be longer than the shortest string.
Check column i across all strings before moving to column i + 1.
Sorting and comparing only the first and last strings is a neat alternative.
pitfalls: Not handling an empty string in the list (answer "").
Index out of range when a later string is shorter than the first.

title: Palindromic Substrings
summary: Count every palindromic substring. Each palindrome has a centre: a character (odd length) or a gap between two characters (even length). Expand outward from all 2n−1 centres, counting each step while the ends match.

complexity.note: Expansion stops at the first mismatch.

intuition: 2n − 1 centres: n single characters and n − 1 gaps.
Expand while `s[l] == s[r]`; each successful expansion is one more palindrome.
No extra space, unlike the DP table.
pitfalls: Counting distinct palindromes instead of all occurrences.

title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
summary: Add words, and search where '.' matches any letter. Store words in a trie. Searching follows the exact child for a letter, and tries every child for a '.', using recursion.

complexity.note: Searches with many dots can branch widely.

intuition: Plain letters follow one path, exactly like a normal trie.
A '.' branches into every existing child.
Return true as soon as any branch finds a word end.
pitfalls: Forgetting to check `isEnd` at the last character.

title: Search Suggestions System
summary: After each typed character, suggest up to three products with that prefix, in alphabetical order. Sort the products once. For each prefix, binary-search the first product ≥ the prefix; the next three products that still start with it are the suggestions.

complexity.average: O(n log n + L log n)
complexity.worst: O(n log n + L log n)
complexity.note: Sorting plus one binary search per typed character.

intuition: In sorted order, all products sharing a prefix are contiguous.
The first one is found by binary search (lower bound).
Take up to three from there while they match the prefix.
A trie storing the top three at each node is the other common solution.
pitfalls: Taking three products without checking they still match the prefix.
input: products = [mobile, mouse, moneypot, monitor, mousepad], searchWord = mouse

def suggestedProducts(products: List[str], searchWord: str) -> List[List[str]]:
    products.sort()
    res, prefix = [], ""
    for c in searchWord:
        prefix += c
        lo = bisect.bisect_left(products, prefix)
        res.append([p for p in products[lo:lo + 3] if p.startswith(prefix)])
    return res

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
summary: Find the longest palindromic substring. Expand from each of the 2n−1 centres while the ends match, and remember the widest expansion seen.

complexity.note: Manacher's algorithm does O(n), but it's rarely expected.

intuition: Odd palindromes centre on a character; even ones on a gap.
Expansion returns the length; convert it back to a start index.
Keep only the best start and length, not the substring.
pitfalls: Off-by-one when converting the expanded bounds back to a substring.

title: Word Search II
summary: Find every dictionary word on the grid. Put all words in a trie and DFS from every cell, walking the trie alongside the grid. A path that leaves the trie is abandoned immediately, so all words are searched at once.

complexity.note: The trie prunes most paths early.

intuition: Searching each word separately repeats work; the trie shares prefixes.
Store the full word at its end node to collect it directly.
Clear the stored word once found so it's not reported twice.
Mark cells with '#' during the DFS and restore them after.
pitfalls: Running Word Search I for every word times out.
Reporting duplicates when a word can be found along two paths.
